# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Martial_2016_caspofungin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Martial_2016_caspofungin"))$description`
* Article (open access, CC BY-NC): <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-015-0347-2>

Martial 2016 developed a population pharmacokinetic model of caspofungin in
intensive care unit (ICU) patients and used it to compare the licensed
maintenance doses (including the label's reduction to 35 mg/day for
Child-Pugh B or C) with three higher-dose alternatives, judged by the day-14
AUC24 and by attainment of the preclinical *Candida albicans* target
AUC/MIC > 865.

# Population

Twenty-one adult ICU patients (8 women, 38%) from a single Dutch study
(NCT01533558) contributed 419 caspofungin concentrations. Median age was 71
years (range 45-80), median weight 75 kg (range 50-99) and median BMI 24.9
kg/m^2 (range 19.0-36.4). All patients were classified Child-Pugh B, all had
hypoalbuminaemia (25-34 g/L in 19%, 15-24 g/L in 68%, < 15 g/L in 14%), and
none were neutropenic. Caspofungin was given for an infection at a normally
sterile site (76%), in blood (19%) or as prophylaxis (5%), as a 70 mg loading
dose followed by 50 mg/day (70 mg/day above 80 kg), each infused over about
1 h (Martial 2016 Table 1 and Methods).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Martial_2016_caspofungin")$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL at 70 kg) | log(0.55) L/h | Table 2 (CL 0.55 L/h [RSE 7%]) |
| `lvc` (V1 at 70 kg) | log(8.93) L | Table 2 (V1 8.93 L [RSE 8%]) |
| `lq` (Q) | log(0.707) L/h | Table 2 (Q 0.707 L/h [RSE 3%]) |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(4.98) L | Table 2 (V2 4.98 L [RSE 17%]) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75, not estimated | Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic Model'; Discussion |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1, not estimated | Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic Model'; Discussion |
| Reference weight | 70 kg | Methods; Table 2 footnote b |
| No weight on Q, V2 | -- | Table 2 footnote c; Discussion (BW on CL and V1) |
| `etalcl` | 30.7% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalvc` | 25.6% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalvp` | 75.8% CV | Table 2 |
| IIV on Q | none (0 in the source) | Table 2 |
| `propSd` | 0.148 | Table 2 |
| `addSd` | 0.01 mg/L, not estimated | Table 2 |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | two-compartment, first-order elimination from central | Results, 'Population Pharmacokinetic Model' |
| `Cc ~ add + prop` | combined residual error | Results, 'Population Pharmacokinetic Model' |
| 1 h IV infusion | dose record (`rate`) | Methods, 'Study Design' |

# Virtual cohort

The paper simulated its regimens in the body weights of 1706 adult hospital
patients (median 76 kg, range 39-154 kg; Methods, 'Monte-Carlo Simulations').
That cohort is not published, so weights here are drawn log-normally with
median 76 kg and a log-scale SD of 0.21, which puts the 1st and 99th
percentiles near 47 and 124 kg, truncated to the published 39-154 kg range.
Each regimen gets 200 subjects.

The five regimens (Methods) are given as 14 daily 1-h infusions:

* I: 70 mg on day 1, then 50 mg/day (BW <= 80 kg) or 70 mg/day (BW > 80 kg)
* II: 70 mg, then 35 mg/day (label for Child-Pugh B or C)
* III: 100 mg, then 50 mg/day
* IV: 100 mg, then 70 mg/day
* V: 100 mg, then 100 mg/day

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2016)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2016)
n_per <- 200L
regimens <- c("I", "II", "III", "IV", "V")
dose_times <- 24 * (0:13)

# Dense sampling over the day-3 (48-72 h) and day-14 (312-336 h) dosing
# intervals for NCA, hourly elsewhere for the concentration-time figure.
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, 336, by = 1),
  seq(48, 72, by = 0.25),
  seq(312, 336, by = 0.25)
)))

regimen_amt <- function(regimen, wt) {
  load <- c(I = 70, II = 70, III = 100, IV = 100, V = 100)[[regimen]]
  maint <- switch(
    regimen,
    I = if (wt <= 80) 50 else 70,
    II = 35,
    III = 50,
    IV = 70,
    V = 100
  )
  c(load, rep(maint, length(dose_times) - 1L))
}

subject_events <- function(id, regimen, wt) {
  amt <- regimen_amt(regimen, wt)
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = dose_times, evid = 1L, amt = amt, rate = amt,
    cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central"
  )
  out <- rbind(doses, obs)
  out$WT <- wt
  out$regimen <- regimen
  out
}

wt_all <- pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_per * length(regimens), log(76), 0.21), 39), 154)
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(wt_all),
  regimen = rep(regimens, each = n_per),
  WT = wt_all
)
events <- do.call(
  rbind,
  Map(subject_events, cohort$id, cohort$regimen, cohort$WT)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

summary(cohort$WT)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Martial_2016_caspofungin")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("regimen", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 4: concentration-time profiles

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 4 of Martial 2016 (median and 5th/95th percentiles over
# 14 days of treatment for regimens I-V).
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% seq(0, 336, by = 1)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    q50 = median(Cc),
    q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = q05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_line(aes(y = q95), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 2, labeller = label_both) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 336, by = 48)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Caspofungin concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Martial 2016: median (solid) and 5th/95th percentiles (dashed)."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

AUC24 over the day-3 (48-72 h) and day-14 (312-336 h) dosing intervals is
computed per subject with PKNCA, grouped by regimen.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 48 & time <= 72 | time >= 312) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, regimen)
dose <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | regimen + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | regimen + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(48, 312),
  end = c(72, 336),
  auclast = TRUE,
  cmax = TRUE,
  cmin = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = ifelse(start == 48, "Day 3", "Day 14"))

auc <- nca |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, day, auc24 = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(cohort |> dplyr::select(id, WT), by = "id")
```

## Steady-state identity

By day 14 every subject is at steady state, where the AUC over one dosing
interval equals the maintenance dose divided by the individual clearance.
Both sides use the same simulated subject, so the only differences are
trapezoidal error and any residual approach to steady state in subjects
with a large peripheral volume.

```{r ss-identity}
indiv_cl <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 312) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, cl)
maint <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 312) |>
  dplyr::select(id, amt)
ss_chk <- auc |>
  dplyr::filter(day == "Day 14") |>
  dplyr::left_join(indiv_cl, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(maint, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc24 / (amt / cl) - 1))
summary(ss_chk$pct_diff)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(ss_chk$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(ss_chk$pct_diff), 0.95) < 3
)
```

## Figure 3: AUC24 by regimen

```{r figure-3}
# Replicates Figure 3 of Martial 2016 (AUC24 on day 3 and day 14 per regimen;
# dashed line at the healthy-volunteer AUC24 of about 100 mg*h/L).
auc |>
  dplyr::mutate(day = factor(day, levels = c("Day 3", "Day 14"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(regimen, auc24)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "grey70", outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~day) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 400)) +
  labs(
    x = "Regimen",
    y = "AUC24 (mg*h/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Martial 2016."
  )
```

## Comparison against the published AUC24

The paper reports median (range) AUC24 for each regimen on days 3 and 14
(Results, 'Monte-Carlo Simulations of Alternative Dosing Regimens').

```{r nca-compare}
published <- data.frame(
  regimen = rep(regimens, 2),
  day = rep(c("Day 3", "Day 14"), each = 5),
  auclast = c(96, 65, 93, 122, 167, 105, 65, 93, 130, 186)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast"),
  reference = published,
  by = c("regimen", "day"),
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Median AUC24: Martial 2016 (Reference) vs this model (Simulated). * differs by > 20%."
)
attr(cmp, "footnote")

typical <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("II", "III", "IV", "V"),
  maintenance_mg = c(35, 50, 70, 100)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    typical_auc = maintenance_mg / (0.55 * (76 / 70)^0.75),
    published = c(65, 93, 130, 186),
    ratio = published / typical_auc
  )
typical |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Maintenance dose (mg)" = maintenance_mg,
    "Dose / CL at 76 kg (mg*h/L)" = typical_auc,
    "Published day-14 median" = published,
    "Published / typical" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Closed-form steady-state AUC24 at the cohort median weight vs the published day-14 medians."
  )
```

The simulated medians sit 5-11% below the published ones (about 8% in the
middle), on both days and in every regimen. The closed-form table shows the
same offset without any simulation: at steady state the median AUC24 is the
maintenance dose over the clearance of a median-weight patient, and the
published day-14 medians are a constant 1.09 times that value. The offset is
therefore not a structural or dosing error in the model but most likely
reflects the unpublished weight distribution of the paper's simulation cohort
(a median weight near 68 kg would reproduce it) or unrounded parameter
estimates. The accumulation from day 3 to day 14, which depends on the
distribution parameters rather than on CL alone, matches the paper: the
day-3/day-14 ratio of the medians is 0.90 for regimen V both here and in the
paper (167/186).

```{r nca-assert}
# Centre-of-distribution check: a mis-transcribed CL, unit or dose moves every
# median by tens of percent; the systematic offset discussed above is ~8%.
auc_pct <- auc |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(auc24), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(published, by = c("regimen", "day")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / auclast - 1))
auc_pct
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_pct$pct_diff)) < 15,
  all(abs(auc_pct$pct_diff) < 25)
)
```

The paper reports a coefficient of variation of the AUC24 of 44-47% for
every regimen; the simulated value is computed below.

```{r auc-cv}
auc |>
  dplyr::group_by(day, regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cv_pct = 100 * sd(auc24) / mean(auc24), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = day, values_from = cv_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated CV% of AUC24 (published: 44-45% on day 3, 46-47% on day 14).")
```

# Target attainment (Figure 5 and Table 3)

Target attainment is the fraction of patients with day-14 AUC24/MIC > 865
(Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic Target Attainment').

```{r pta}
mics <- c(0.007, 0.016, 0.03, 0.06, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1)
d14 <- auc |> dplyr::filter(day == "Day 14")
pta <- tidyr::expand_grid(d14, mic = mics) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    bw_group = ifelse(WT <= 80, "BW <= 80 kg", "BW > 80 kg"),
    hit = auc24 / mic > 865
  )

pta_all <- pta |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, mic) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta = 100 * mean(hit), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(pta_all, aes(mic, pta, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics) +
  labs(
    x = "MIC (ug/mL)",
    y = "Target attainment (%)",
    colour = "Regimen",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Martial 2016 (AUC/MIC > 865)."
  )
```

```{r pta-table}
published_pta <- data.frame(
  regimen = c("I", "II", "III", "IV", "V"),
  published = c(47, 14, 36, 69, 94)
)
pta_all |>
  dplyr::filter(mic == 0.125) |>
  dplyr::left_join(published_pta, by = "regimen") |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, pta, published) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Simulated (%)" = pta,
    "Published (%)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Target attainment at MIC 0.125 ug/mL (published values: Abstract).")

pta |>
  dplyr::filter(mic %in% c(0.06, 0.125, 0.25)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, bw_group, mic) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta = 100 * mean(hit), n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = mic, values_from = pta, names_prefix = "MIC ") |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen, "Body weight" = bw_group, "N" = n) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Simulated target attainment (%) by body-weight group; compare with Table 3 of Martial 2016.")
```

```{r pta-assert}
# The paper's conclusion: at MIC 0.125 the 100/100 mg regimen (V) attains
# the target far more often than the label's 35 mg reduction (II), published
# 94% vs 14%. Model-true values here are near 90% and under 5%; with 200 subjects
# per regimen a binomial SE is at most 3.5 points, so a 50-point margin is
# many SEs from either side.
p125 <- setNames(pta_all$pta[pta_all$mic == 0.125], pta_all$regimen[pta_all$mic == 0.125])
stopifnot(p125[["V"]] - p125[["II"]] > 50)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **CL-V1 correlation not encoded.** The Results state that allowing a
  correlation between the IIV of CL and V1 improved the fit (OFV drop 8.6),
  but no correlation or covariance value is reported in Table 2 or the text,
  and the article has no supplement. The IIV is encoded as diagonal. At
  steady state the AUC24 depends on CL only, so the AUC and
  target-attainment results are unaffected; peak concentrations would be
  slightly more variable with the correlation omitted.
- **IIV and residual error conventions.** Table 2 reports IIV as CV%; the
  variances are `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The proportional residual error
  (0.148) is read as a standard deviation (14.8%), and the additive term
  (0.01 mg/L, not estimated) as a standard deviation in mg/L, matching the
  units printed in the table.
- **Weight scaling of Q and V2.** The Methods say weight was included on CL
  and 'Vd'; the Discussion specifies CL (exponent 0.75) and V1 (exponent 1),
  and Table 2 footnote c says Q and V2 are 'scaled to the mean of the
  population' while footnote b says CL and V1 are standardised to 70 kg. The
  model therefore applies weight to CL and V1 only, with Q and V2 at their
  population typical values.
- **Simulation cohort.** The paper simulated the weights of 1706 hospital
  patients (median 76 kg, range 39-154 kg); the individual weights are not
  published, so a log-normal distribution with that median, truncated to that
  range, is used with 200 subjects per regimen rather than one 1706-patient
  cohort. The paper's AUC24 medians are a constant 8-9% above the closed-form
  steady-state value at 76 kg (see the comparison above), which points to a
  difference in the weight distribution or unrounded estimates rather than
  in model structure. The simulated AUC24 CV% (about 29-37%) is also lower
  than the published 44-47%; a CL IIV of 30.7% CV combined with the weight
  spread cannot produce a 45% CV of AUC24 at steady state, so the paper's
  simulation must have carried additional variability (for example a wider
  weight distribution or residual error in the simulated concentrations)
  that is not described. Together with the lower median, this places the
  simulated target attainment at MIC 0.125 ug/mL 2-12 percentage points
  below the published values, with the same ranking of regimens.
- **Residual error in AUC.** AUC24 here is computed from the individual
  predictions (`Cc`) without residual error; the paper does not say whether
  its AUCs included residual error.
- **Errata.** No correction notice is linked to the article in its PubMed
  Central record (checked 2026-11-24).
